title: ClaimScope fictional evidence demo
notice: Every document and claim below is invented for UI and retrieval demonstration. None is a real study or scientific result.

documents.title: A fictional comparison of retrieval strategies
documents.text: In a simulated collection of 600 questions, a hybrid lexical and dense retrieval system achieved recall at five of 0.82, while a BM25-only baseline achieved 0.75. These illustrative values are invented for the ClaimScope demo and are not empirical research.

documents.title: A fictional note on evidence and causality
documents.text: The toy analysis reports an association between the retrieval configuration and the measured recall. It did not randomize systems, test statistical significance, or establish that hybrid retrieval causes improved performance.

documents.title: A fictional model evaluation record
documents.text: The example classifier was evaluated on a synthetic dataset created solely for a software demonstration. No patients or students were studied, and no clinical outcome or diagnostic label was used.

documents.title: A fictional model evaluation record
documents.text: On the invented validation split, the toy classifier had macro F1 of 0.71. This result is a fabricated placeholder for demonstrating how a claim may be linked to evidence; it must not be cited as a real performance finding.

documents.title: A fictional retrieval ablation
documents.text: Removing the reranking stage reduced recall at five from 0.82 to 0.78 in this invented example. The toy setup does not include repeated seeds or confidence intervals.

documents.title: A fictional evidence boundary
documents.text: A passage may share words with a claim and still fail to support it. Topical similarity and lexical overlap are retrieval signals, not entailment or proof.
